title: Togo's Novissi program targeted rural emergency cash with machine learning on satellite imagery and mobile-phone data
summary: ML on satellite imagery and phone metadata set eligibility for Novissi rural cash; 138,531 beneficiaries paid, Nov 2020 to Aug 2021
account: The Government of Togo launched the Novissi emergency cash program on 8 April 2020. On 2 November 2020 it extended it to rural areas using a machine-learning pipeline built with UC Berkeley and IPA researchers. Satellite imagery produced poverty estimates for every canton to rank the poorest. Within eligible cantons a model trained on mobile-phone metadata predicted each subscriber's consumption to decide who was paid. Beneficiaries self-registered by USSD and received mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men). The World Bank and Government of Togo report 138,531 rural beneficiaries from November 2020 to August 2021, funded by GiveDirectly (US$10 million). The Nature evaluation found that phone-based targeting reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives. In a hypothetical comparison with methods requiring a comprehensive social registry, which Togo did not have, phone-based targeting increased exclusion errors by 9–35%.
purpose: Prioritize the poorest cantons and the poorest mobile subscribers within them for COVID-19 emergency cash transfers in the absence of a social registry.
system: Novissi rural targeting pipeline: satellite-imagery poverty maps for canton ranking plus supervised machine learning on anonymized mobile-phone call detail records for individual eligibility
model_version: gradient boosting regressor with Microsoft's LightGBM
developer: Innovations for Poverty Action, CEGA and UC Berkeley (Aiken and Blumenstock, UC Berkeley; Bellue, University of Mannheim; Karlan and Udry, Northwestern University) for the Government of Togo
deployer: Government of Togo, Ministry of Digital Economy and Transformation, with GiveDirectly
domain: Social protection and humanitarian cash transfers
taxonomy_note: The good for beneficiaries is emergency cash, and the type names the program's reach into rural areas with no registry.

ratings.reason: Five mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men) to each of 138,531 rural beneficiaries during COVID-19 restrictions (World Bank study, Table 1).
The Government of Togo delivered shock-responsive rural assistance without a social registry. The World Bank documents the model as a reusable case study.
Material to many: 138,531 rural beneficiaries reached, and the Nature evaluation reports exclusion errors 4–21% lower than geographic targeting.

ai_role.statement: Decisive for who was paid: canton ranking and individual eligibility were both set by machine-learning predictions, while humans fixed the budget, thresholds and registration rules. The Nature evaluation is co-authored by the team that built the targeting method. The World Bank/Government of Togo case study is independent of the developers.

fields.account: The Government of Togo launched the Novissi emergency cash program on 8 April 2020. On 2 November 2020 it extended it to rural areas using a machine-learning pipeline built with UC Berkeley and IPA researchers. Satellite imagery produced poverty estimates for every canton to rank the poorest. Within eligible cantons a model trained on mobile-phone metadata predicted each subscriber's consumption to decide who was paid. Beneficiaries self-registered by USSD and received mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men). The World Bank and Government of Togo report 138,531 rural beneficiaries from November 2020 to August 2021, funded by GiveDirectly (US$10 million). The Nature evaluation found that phone-based targeting reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives. In a hypothetical comparison with methods requiring a comprehensive social registry, which Togo did not have, phone-based targeting increased exclusion errors by 9–35%.

fields.account: The Government of Togo launched the Novissi emergency cash program on 8 April 2020. On 2 November 2020 it extended it to rural areas using a machine-learning pipeline built with UC Berkeley and IPA researchers. Satellite imagery produced poverty estimates for every canton to rank the poorest. Within eligible cantons a model trained on mobile-phone metadata predicted each subscriber's consumption to decide who was paid. Beneficiaries self-registered by USSD and received mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men). The World Bank and Government of Togo report 138,531 rural beneficiaries from November 2020 to August 2021, funded by GiveDirectly (US$10 million). The Nature evaluation found that phone-based targeting reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives. In a hypothetical comparison with methods requiring a comprehensive social registry, which Togo did not have, phone-based targeting increased exclusion errors by 9–35%.
